title: Three-minute drift bisect and ad-hoc rubric (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for a fast triage session — noticed an uptick in short-response truncation after the 2025-02-10 deploy. Small sample check (customer-facing chat routes) shows more frequent premature stops on follow-ups and increased 'I don't know' tokens. This is a personal notebook for running a fast bisect and sketching an ad-hoc rubric that we can ship to QA for a short-run sweep.

Observations (raw):
- Spike in truncated responses observed between 2025-02-10 02:00 and 2025-02-10 04:30 UTC (per sampling job ml-sampler-42).
- Regression signal strongest on short-context prompts (<100 tokens), multi-turn.
- Hypothesis: change in kernel scheduling + new batching heuristics leading to early EOS emission in certain quantized model variant (q8) on dedicated pool A.
- Secondary hypothesis: prefix cache miss pattern causing shorter generated continuations due to cache warm-up.

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (for quick human labels, 1–3 min per sample):
- Relevance (R): 0/1 — reply addresses user's most recent turn?
- Completeness (C): 0/2 — 0 = abruptly truncated / unfinished clause; 1 = missing minor detail; 2 = fully complete for the prompt intent.
- Hallucination flag (H): 0/1 — introduces unsupported fact?
- Latency note (L): short|ok|slow (free-text if abnormal)
- Confidence (Q): quick freeform: "likely regression", "looks normal", "need model trace"

Scoring example (annotator instructions):
- Score = R + C (max 3). Anything <=1 => immediate triage.
- If H==1 and Score<=2 => mark high priority.

Sample prompts + outputs (copied verbatim from sampler run id=ml-sampler-42, batch 13):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the last message: 'I got the invoice but the total looks off — the discount isn't applied'"
   Output (old-stable): "You should check the invoice line items — the discount code might not have been applied to the subtotal. Can you share the invoice id?"
   Output (post-deploy q8): "Check the invoice id."  <-- truncated, incomplete, Score R=1, C=0, H=0

2) Prompt: "How do I revoke an API key in the console?"
   Output (old-stable): "Settings > API keys, click revoke next to the key. Note: revocation is immediate and affects running sessions."
   Output (post-deploy q8): "Settings > API keys."  <-- abrupt, Score=R=1, C=0

3) Prompt (edge): multi-turn follow-up that expects referent resolution.
   Output (post-deploy q8): "I don't know."  <-- new failure mode: safe-answer proliferation

First-pass bisect notes (what I ran):
- Rolled back worker-kernel-pkg to v2.1.7 on canary; re-ran sampler; failure rate on small-context tests dropped from 18% -> 4% (n=250 samples).
- Force-quantized-run on dedicated pool B with old kernel shows improved completeness.
- Canary with new batching policy + old kernel gave intermediate results (12% failure).

Preliminary attribution: new kernel scheduling change in v2.1.8 interacts with continuous-batching heuristics that shorten attention window in certain micro-batches (on q8). The quick rollback suggests kernel change is main factor; batching policy amplifies but not primary.

Immediate next steps (for this afternoon):
- Replicate with deterministic seeds: run ml-sampler-42 with seed=20250301 across kernels 2.1.7/2.1.8 and batching on/off (script: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/quick-bisect.sh). (Assigned to: Imogen)
- Capture kv-cache traces and EOS token probability deltas for 50 failing examples (Assigned: Liam). Add log flag eos-debug=true in dev: canary config.
- Short human sweep using the micro-rubric above (n=100) -> send to QA channel and link results to JIRA-ML-1038. (Assigned: Maya)
- If replicable, draft rollback playbook snippet for ops and open a rollback RFC to revert kernel change for dedicated A until fixed.

Longer-term hypotheses to validate (notes):
- Quantization path may have lower numerical stability at small sequence lengths causing early EOS. Run numeric sensitivity tests on q4/q8/q6 with synthetic sequences.
- Batching heuristics that rely on estimated remaining length might mis-estimate in presence of prefix-cache misses; consider conservative lower bound for remaining tokens in mixed-tenant pool.

Quick checklist (for the triage call):
- [ ] Confirm regression window & deploy SHA per region (asia/north-america/eu)
- [ ] Attach failing sample IDs to JIRA-ML-1038
- [ ] Share minimal reproduction and kernel config diff to infra-cc
- [ ] Decide rollback threshold (failure rate >10% on short-context multi-turn)

Loose notes / stray hypotheses:
- Could also be a tokenization boundary change in tokeniser-lib v0.9.2 (we updated that in same release). Quick test: run tokenized-length histogram on samples pre/post.
- Look for correlated uptick in generator eos-prob mean metric in console traces (per-route heatmap).

Notes to self (format to hand off to QA):
- Keep the rubric very short (R 0/1, C 0/2, H 0/1). Don't ask for lengthier writeups — we need throughput.
- Provide annotators with baseline "good" and "bad" examples (use the two samples above).

End-of-scratchpad. Will convert to a more formal triage doc once the deterministic runs finish.
